target_customer: Lenders, card issuers and landlords that pay to access imported international credit data on newcomers (later also cash flow underwriting customers)
problem: Immigrants lose their credit history when they move to the US, so even people with good histories abroad cannot get cards or loans.
business_model: B2B usage-based fees charged to lenders per report, similar to how Experian and Equifax charge
product_category: Cross-border credit data and underwriting infrastructure (consumer reporting agency)

founders.name: Misha Esipov
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says his parents moved from Russia in 1990.

founders.name: Nicky Goulimis
founders.background_notes: Described as a Bain consultant by TechCrunch. Not listed on the YC company page, named by TechCrunch, Index Ventures and the 2020 funding article.

founders.name: Loek Janssen
founders.background_notes: Described as a full-stack developer by TechCrunch.

competitors.name: Experian and Equifax (US credit bureaus)
competitors.what: Incumbent bureaus that sell US credit reports to lenders; Nova copied their per-report pricing model but filled the gap for newcomers with no US file

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed data partnerships with foreign bureaus and mapping foreign scores to US-style reports, plus FCRA compliance; engineering was standard but integrations were hard.

defensibility.rationale: Bureau data partnerships across countries and consumer reporting agency compliance took years to replicate, as shown by later partners such as American Express.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of incumbents shipping the same cross-border product in 2016; Nova became a partner to banks and issuers instead.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in Aug 2016 cited roughly 15 million immigrants arriving in the US with no practical way to access credit.

branding.domain_note: Uses novacredit.com; no acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-driven financial inclusion; tagline The Power to Underwrite Anyone

branding.brand_signature: Credit Passport (trademarked product name, registration dated 2017-05 per a third-party database)
branding.community_and_virality: No merch or fan community found; brand mostly noted through bank partner announcements.

brand_strength.rationale: Credit Passport is a memorable product name that conveys the idea, but the company name is generic and shared with other Nova brands, such as Nova Launcher.

pivots.to: Broader cash flow underwriting and income verification (Cash Atlas, Income Navigator)
pivots.why: Expansion beyond immigrants into alternative data, per company site and TechCrunch Oct 2023 headline

outcome_analysis: Nova Credit launched at YC Demo Day 2016 on a problem all three founders had lived, signed Index as a first investor, then raised a Series A in 2018 and a 50 million dollar Series B in 2020. It later broadened to cash flow underwriting and raised a Series C in 2023 and a Series D in 2025. It remains active with about 100 staff.
notes: Series A 16 million dollars with Index and General Catalyst is from a search summary of aggregator listings; Index's own post confirms Series A (May 2018) but states no amount. Seed amount is conflicting across aggregator profiles (3 to 4.9 million) so unverified and not recorded. TechCrunch Feb 2020 says just under 20 million raised before Series B including YC. Co-founder roles of Goulimis from an engine.is title. Outcome search found no shutdown, layoffs or acquisition for this company.
